content.comment_body: Is it possible to connect expansion modules with varying voltage levels to a [product_name] Basis Module? For instance: [product_name] Basis 230 > [product_name] Digital 24 > [product_name] Digital 230, or [product_name] Basis 230 > [product_name] Digital 230 > [product_name] Digital 24, or [product_name] Basis 24 > [product_name] Digital 24 > [product_name] Digital 230, or [product_name] Basis 24 > [product_name] Digital 230 > [product_name] Digital 24.

It is possible, but only under specific conditions. A 12/24 VDC expansion module can be added to a 230 VAC base or extension module if an analog module is placed first, then the 12/24 VDC module. However, you cannot place a 230 VAC module after a 12/24 VDC or an analog module. Please refer to the attached diagram.

If the [product_name] 12/24 operates with a 12VDC power supply and the [product_name] Digital 24 runs on a separate 24VDC power supply, is it possible to connect them together as follows? [product_name] 12/24 > [product_name] Digital 24

analysis.insight_summary: There is uncertainty around how expansion modules with differing voltage ratings can be combined with a [product_name] Basis Module. The discussion highlights issues with module arrangement, voltage compatibility, and whether separate power supplies allow such configurations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are hoping to mix expansion modules that require different voltages on a single [product_name] Basis Module, potentially supplying each module with an independent power source.
